description: The OpenQuake Engine is the seismic hazard and risk calculation software developed by the Global Earthquake Model (GEM) Foundation, designed as an open, community-driven tool. It implements probabilistic and scenario-based seismic hazard analysis (hazard curves, maps, uniform hazard spectra, disaggregation, event-based ground-motion fields) and risk calculators for damage and losses to exposed assets using fragility and vulnerability functions, including classical and event-based damage and risk, multi-peril scenario damage and retrofit benefit-cost ratios, reading source, exposure and vulnerability models as input files. It runs as a command-line engine on a laptop or on multiple nodes and SLURM clusters, with a web user interface, is installed from PyPI (openquake-engine 3.26.2) or installers, and the code is licensed AGPL-3.0-or-later at no cost, while the manual is CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 and many GEM models carry their own licences. Caveats: hazard and risk models must be supplied by the user or obtained from GEM under their own terms, calculations can be memory-heavy, and it covers earthquake and some secondary perils, not all hazards. It is used for hazard exposure of infrastructure and lifelines, fragility-based damage and resilience analysis, and pairs with the GEM global seismic hazard map and with loss frameworks such as Oasis LMF.
